content.title: Perplexity
content.text: $43.233.72% at Close · $43.190.09% After HoursProShares UltraPro QQQ rallied sharply, buoyed by a broad Nasdaq surge as geopolitical optimism around the U.S.-Iran conflict drove a powerful risk-on rotation into high-beta tech assets. The 3x leveraged ETF amplified gains across its top holdings — NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Tesla, and Meta — as President Trump signaled the war could end within two to three weeks, sending oil prices below $100 and lifting growth stocks broadly. The S&P 500 gained nearly 1% on April 1, extending Tuesday's best single-day rally since May, while institutional interest in TQQQ has been notably rising, with major firms like Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Cantor Fitzgerald dramatically increasing positions in recent quarters.$41.6810.00% ProShares UltraPro QQQ surged alongside Wall Street's best single-day rally in nearly a year, as Iran's president signaled willingness to end hostilities with the U.S., sparking a sharp drop in oil prices and a risk-on rotation back into tech. The Nasdaq Composite closed up ~3.8% and the S&P 500 gained ~2.9%, amplified roughly threefold in TQQQ given its 3x leveraged structure; volume came in well above average as traders piled into the leveraged ETF, with the ETF continuing to gain in after-hours trade. Several large institutions — including Cantor Fitzgerald, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs — had recently disclosed substantial new or expanded TQQQ positions, reflecting growing institutional appetite for leveraged Nasdaq exposure ahead of the geopolitically driven relief rally.$37.892.29% ProShares UltraPro QQQ fell roughly 2.3% as the Nasdaq slid for a third consecutive session amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran war now in its fifth week, with oil closing above $100 per barrel for the first time since 2022. As a 3x leveraged NASDAQ-100 ETF, TQQQ amplified broad tech weakness driven by surging energy prices, inflation fears, and semiconductor pressure—Micron fell nearly 10% on Google's TurboQuant concerns while Apple and other top holdings also declined. In after-hours trading, the fund extended losses an additional 1.2%, reflecting continued geopolitical anxiety as Iran struck a Kuwaiti crude carrier, driving S&P 500 futures lower and crude oil up another 3.4%.$38.785.94% ProShares UltraPro QQQ tumbled nearly 6% — its most pronounced single-session decline in weeks — as the Nasdaq entered correction territory amid escalating U.S.-Iran war tensions and surging oil prices above $100/barrel. The 3x leveraged NASDAQ-100 ETF magnified broad tech-sector losses driven by Iran's rejection of ceasefire proposals, spiking Treasury yields (10-year at 4.44%), and growing stagflation fears, with the Dow closing in correction territory for a fifth straight week of losses. After-hours pressure continued, with the fund extending its decline to nearly 1.5% in extended trading.$41.237.12% ProShares UltraPro QQQ tumbled on Thursday as the S&P 500 posted its worst single-day decline since the Iran war began, falling 1.7% and pushing the Nasdaq into correction territory with a 2.4% drop. As a 3x leveraged NASDAQ-100 ETF, TQQQ amplified those losses sharply, with volume spiking above 112 million shares versus its 97 million average. Iran's continued rejection of Trump's 15-point ceasefire proposal — and oil prices surging toward $108/barrel — fueled the risk-off selloff, while BlackRock's downgrade of U.S. equities to 'neutral' underscored the macro headwinds investors now face.$44.391.77% ProShares UltraPro QQQ rose nearly 2% as the Nasdaq gained 0.8% on cautious optimism around a potential U.S.-Iran ceasefire. A U.S. 15-point peace plan sent to Iran via Pakistan lifted risk sentiment and pushed oil prices sharply lower, benefiting Nasdaq-heavy tech names like Nvidia, Apple, and Tesla — all key holdings of this 3x leveraged ETF. While Iran rejected the proposal and gains were pared from morning highs above $45, the fund still closed higher as investors weighed de-escalation hopes against persistent geopolitical volatility and elevated oil prices that have kept rate-cut expectations suppressed.$43.622.13% ProShares UltraPro QQQ fell over 2% as renewed Middle East uncertainty whipsawed Nasdaq-100 underlying holdings — oil rebounded above $100/bbl after Iran denied the "productive talks" claimed by Trump, erasing much of Monday's relief rally. The 3x leveraged ETF's top holdings (NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, TSLA) all came under pressure amid rising bond yields and private-credit liquidity concerns, while after-hours futures climbed ~2.45% on reports the U.S. sent Iran a 15-point peace plan, hinting at potential de-escalation.$44.573.46% ProShares UltraPro QQQ gained roughly 3.5%, amplifying a broad market relief rally triggered by President Trump's surprise announcement pausing strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure for five days and citing 'productive' talks with Tehran. As a 3x leveraged Nasdaq-100 ETF, TQQQ magnified the NASDAQ's ~1.4% advance, with the fund trading well above average volume amid wild intraday swings — markets initially surged over 2% on the news before retreating as Iran's foreign ministry denied any talks had taken place. Despite closing well off intraday highs, the S&P 500 posted its best day since the conflict began, and TQQQ continued to edge higher in after-hours trading as Asian markets prepared to rebound on the de-escalation signal.$43.085.71% ProShares UltraPro QQQ tumbled sharply as escalating Middle East conflict drove Brent crude past $110/barrel, reigniting stagflation fears and pushing the S&P 500 below its 200-day moving average for the first time in nearly a year — the Nasdaq's fourth consecutive weekly loss of 3.1%. The 3x leveraged ETF amplified the Nasdaq-100's roughly 1.3% decline, while above-average volume (~131M shares vs. 94M average) reflected heightened retail trader activity; in after-hours trading, shares are recovering modestly as oil prices ease and broader sentiment stabilizes.$45.690.89% ProShares UltraPro QQQ closed modestly lower as a broad risk-off wave swept through Nasdaq-heavy assets, driven by the escalating Middle East energy crisis and a hawkish Federal Reserve posture. With Brent crude briefly topping $119 a barrel after Iranian strikes on Qatar's LNG infrastructure, inflation fears spiked and the Fed — holding rates steady at 3.5-3.75% and signaling only one cut in 2026 — further dashed hopes for near-term policy easing, pressuring the leveraged tech-index ETF's top holdings including NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, and TSLA. Trading volume surged well above average, and the fund edged up 0.53% in after-hours trade as oil retreated from its intraday highs.$46.104.28% ProShares UltraPro QQQ fell sharply, amplifying the Nasdaq's 1.5% decline after the Federal Reserve held rates steady while signaling only one potential cut for the year amid hotter-than-expected PPI inflation data. The triple-leveraged ETF's 4.28% drop reflected a 3x magnification of Nasdaq-100 weakness driven by Fed Chair Powell's hawkish inflation commentary, a surge in Brent crude above $110/barrel following Israeli strikes on Iran's South Pars gas field, and growing stagflation concerns that pressured mega-cap tech holdings including Nvidia, Apple, and Meta.$48.161.47% ProShares UltraPro QQQ rose modestly, benefiting from a second consecutive day of Nasdaq gains as investors grew more comfortable looking past the Iran conflict's energy shock. The broader tech rebound was fueled by Nvidia's GTC 2026 keynote — where Jensen Huang projected $1 trillion in AI chip demand through 2027 — alongside Meta's workforce cut reports and the Uber-Nvidia robotaxi expansion, with all eyes turning to the Fed's rate decision Wednesday. Short interest in TQQQ fell 26% in February, suggesting reduced bearish positioning ahead of the relief rally.$47.463.33% ProShares UltraPro QQQ gained over 3% as a broad market relief rally took hold, with the Nasdaq leading major indexes higher after oil prices pulled back from recent highs tied to the Iran-Strait of Hormuz crisis. The day's advance was fueled by strong AI momentum — Nvidia's GTC conference announcements, Meta's workforce reduction plans aimed at offsetting AI costs, and Micron's new Taiwan facility — while short interest in TQQQ dropped 26% in February, signaling reduced bearish conviction. Investors are watching Wednesday's Fed meeting closely, with rate-cut expectations now pushed to beyond October.$45.931.92% ProShares UltraPro QQQ fell nearly 2%, amplifying the Nasdaq's 0.93% decline as the ongoing U.S.-Israel war with Iran kept oil near $100/barrel and stoked stagflation fears. The S&P 500 marked consecutive weekly losses while key TQQQ holdings — NVDA, META, TSLA, AMZN, and GOOGL — all declined, with TQQQ's 3x leverage translating those losses into outsized pressure; the fund saw notable outflows of ~$267M the prior session, reflecting investor caution toward leveraged tech exposure in the current macro environment.$46.835.11% ProShares UltraPro QQQ tumbled as a surge in oil prices above $100/barrel amid the ongoing U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran rattled global equity markets, sending the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to their lowest closes of 2026. As a 3x leveraged Nasdaq-100 ETF, TQQQ amplified the tech-heavy index's decline, with volume running well above average as investors shed risk assets; the leveraged ETF space broadly saw outflows while investors rotated toward energy and defensive sectors.$49.350.10% ProShares UltraPro QQQ closed essentially flat but slipped further in after-hours trading, declining over 2%, as Wall Street remained on edge over surging oil prices tied to the ongoing Iran conflict. Despite softer February CPI data (2.4% YoY), markets largely looked past the inflation print as energy shock fears dominated sentiment, with Brent crude closing above $91 and 10-year Treasury yields climbing to a month-long high above 4.20%. Options activity on TQQQ remained elevated, with 1.53 million contracts in open interest and nearly 286K contracts traded, as investors use the 3x-leveraged Nasdaq ETF to hedge or express directional bets on big tech and AI names like Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft — all top holdings.$49.400.02% ProShares UltraPro QQQ closed essentially unchanged as markets navigated a volatile session driven by the ongoing U.S.-Iran war and its impact on oil prices. Crude oil tumbled roughly 10% to ~$85/barrel after G-7 nations discussed releasing strategic reserves and Trump signaled the conflict was 'very complete, pretty much,' helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq hold gains. TQQQ's top holding NVIDIA rose modestly on continued AI demand enthusiasm ahead of the GTC conference, while Oracle beat earnings and surged after-hours, providing a tailwind for tech sentiment.$49.393.89% ProShares UltraPro QQQ surged 3.89% to close at $49.39, recapturing ground as the underlying Nasdaq-100 recovered from morning lows driven by Middle East tensions and oil-market volatility. The ETF—whose top holdings include IQMM (28.5%), NVDA (5.0%), AAPL (4.4%), and MSFT (3.5%)—amplifies moves in the tech-heavy index by 3x daily. After falling over 5% intraday to $45.50 amid a global risk-off rout sparked by crude-oil prices surging past $100 (up ~25–30% on supply disruptions from the U.S.–Israel–Iran conflict), TQQQ rebounded with a late-session rally as markets digested President Trump's comment that the war is 'very complete, pretty complete' and oil futures pulled back from $120 highs to settle near $94–$105 by New York close. Volume spiked to 156.9 million shares, 68% above average, while sector-peer XLF edged lower and the S&P 500 trimmed earlier 1.6% losses to finish -0.5%. Investors are now watching whether today's relief rally can hold, or whether stagflation risks from rising energy prices and weak payroll data (February nonfarm employment fell 92k, unemployment 4.4%) prompt further profit-taking in leveraged tech positions.$47.544.54% ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) closed sharply lower, falling 4.54% to $47.54 as broader market weakness intensified amid surging oil prices and weak U.S. jobs data. The decline reflected heavy selling in technology-leveraged products as investors reacted to a surprise February payroll contraction of 92,000 jobs and elevated crude oil prices (WTI above $89, Brent above $90), which together raised stagflation concerns and complicated the Federal Reserve's policy path. The drop extended TQQQ's underperformance relative to its underlying Nasdaq-100 exposure, with elevated volatility driven by above-average volume (140 million shares vs. 92 million average) as traders rotated out of leveraged risk assets.$49.800.92% ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) closed down 0.92% at $49.80 as the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.48% and the S&P 500 declined 0.30%. The leveraged ETF's drop reflected triple-amplified exposure to the Nasdaq 100's retreat amid surging oil prices (WTI crude up over 5% toward $79 per barrel) and escalating Middle East tensions following an Iranian missile strike on an oil tanker and ongoing conflict in the Persian Gulf. Geopolitical risk and inflation fears—driven by oil's jump to its highest level since June 2025—pressured tech-heavy growth stocks and overshadowed strong tech earnings from Broadcom and Trade Desk. Heavy trading volume (127.8M shares vs 91.1M average) and sector rotation into value and defensive names further weighed on the triple-leveraged Nasdaq fund.$50.264.49% TQQQ surged 4.49% to close at $50.26 as markets bounced from a multi‑day selloff driven by U.S.–Iran geopolitical tensions. Tech stocks and the Nasdaq rallied after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced plans to secure oil shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, easing supply-disruption fears. Iran sent diplomatic signals via a third-party intelligence agency, and better-than-expected U.S. jobs and services data reinforced economic resilience. Options activity remained elevated—292,390 contracts traded—and analysts highlighted that the rebound reflected a shift from panic to cautious optimism, as falling oil prices and short‑term de‑escalation hopes lifted risk appetite.$48.103.22% TQQQ closed down 3.22% at $48.10 as global market risk-off and escalating U.S.-Israel-Iran tensions pressured tech and leveraged funds. The 3x Nasdaq-tracking ETF dropped alongside tech peers after geopolitical fears drove oil above $80, VIX to 27, and the S&P 500 down nearly 2% intraday. Short interest in TQQQ had surged 38% to 30.8M shares by mid-February, signaling heavy bearish positioning ahead of the selloff. Institutional buyers including Cassaday & Co and Clarity Wealth had been adding exposure in Q3, but the conflict and oil shock erased recent gains and lifted volatility across leveraged products.$49.700.36% ProShares UltraPro QQQ closed up 0.36% at $49.70, recovering from intraday lows as geopolitical tensions sent markets into risk-off mode before a tech-led rebound took hold. The 3x leveraged Nasdaq fund saw above-average volume of 107 million shares amid escalating Middle East conflict, rising oil prices, and lingering AI disruption fears. Investors rotated into defense and energy names early—pushing Palantir and Exxon higher—while semiconductor and software stocks swung sharply; Nvidia gained 3% intraday, helping lift TQQQ off session lows. Short interest surged 38% in February to 5.7% of shares outstanding, and institutional flows were mixed, reflecting heightened volatility as the market absorbed both war risk and sticky inflation signals.
